phase.documentation: accepted corrections/subsets edited, independently reviewed and validated in ../oath-003-004
phase.remaining: implementation and contract portions remain deferred; individual statuses below preserve triage disposition

verification: Source/test reading and primary-specification comparison; no execution during this investigation

findings.evidence: Code sets HOTP only for TagHotp. YKOATH distinguishes HOTP and touch markers.
findings.disposition: Correct comment, retaining LIST versus CALCULATE ALL name-byte distinction. Do not assert marker precedence for touch-required HOTP.

findings.location: IOathSession.CalculateAsync; OathSession.cs:398-413; CLAUDE.md user-presence validation claim
findings.claim: Full HMAC return and blanket CALCULATE validation claim conflict with actual returned TLV bytes.
findings.evidence: YKOATH full response value contains digit byte plus HMAC. Source returns entire value and completes after tag presence alone; empty values also succeed. Existing full-response fixtures are not protocol-shaped.
findings.disposition: Implement validated full-response parsing and intended HMAC-only return at closeout; replace unrealistic fixtures. Safely qualify/remove blanket contributor validation claim now without redefining header-inclusive output as the intended public contract.

findings.claim: Malformed semantic responses can index missing data, be silently dropped, or become null results.
findings.evidence: LIST assumes leading algorithm byte. Aggregate silently drops unmatched last TLV, skips wrong name tags, maps unknown tags to null, and recalculates custom periods before validating initial value. Generic TLV decoding validates encoding only.
findings.disposition: Define required response structure and meaningful failures, preserving intended forward extension handling. Do not normalize missing required data as partial success.
findings.confidence: high for source branches; extension/duplicate policy unresolved

findings.claim: Malformed IDs generally are omitted and logged.
findings.evidence: The parser rejects recognized zero/overflow ASCII TOTP period prefixes but accepts/falls back on other unusual names; it does not comprehensively validate raw IDs.
findings.disposition: Describe invalid recognized TOTP period prefixes precisely, linking shared explanation where useful. Do not tighten runtime response handling.

findings.claim: ValidFrom/ValidTo describe verifier validity; HOTP never expires.
findings.evidence: Code computes nominal TOTP generation-window bounds; HOTP uses requested/current timestamp and long.MaxValue. RFC6238 verifier windows/drift/reuse and RFC4226 counters mean these are not perpetual/exact acceptance guarantees.
findings.disposition: Define inclusive/exclusive TOTP generation-window metadata and HOTP no-time-expiry sentinel, not verifier acceptance. Avoid asserting support for unresolved timestamp extremes.

findings.location: IOathSession calculation methods; README calculation guide
findings.claim: Calculation docs omit HOTP side effects and timestamp applicability.
findings.evidence: TOTP challenge uses Unix seconds; HOTP sends empty challenge but stores timestamp as Code.ValidFrom. Integration source expects successive HOTP calculations to advance; RFC4226 section7.4 describes counter advancement, but consulted YKOATH does not detail full/truncated failure timing.
findings.disposition: Document timestamp units/default and metadata role now. Hold device-specific full/truncated counter consumption and failure guarantees for closeout evidence; do not imply failed calls cannot advance counters.
findings.confidence: high for timestamp source; device timing unresolved

findings.location: OathSession.cs:615-625 ResetAsync; IOathSession reset contract; ResetCommand error output
findings.claim: A reset failure can occur after destructive RESET already succeeded.
findings.evidence: RESET and subsequent SELECT are separate token-aware exchanges; state refresh occurs only after SELECT parsing. Cancellation or refresh failure can leave erased device data and stale session state.
findings.disposition: Track state invalidation/recovery and SCP-reset investigation. A short factual partial-success warning/reopen recommendation may be documented now without promising a recovery mechanism or rollback.
findings.confidence: high for source boundary; SCP behavior needs device evidence

findings.location: OathSession timestamp division; Code.cs:89-93; public timestamp parameters
findings.claim: Timestamp domain is unspecified despite signed-division and overflow edge cases.
findings.evidence: -1/30 truncates to zero, unlike RFC6238 floor; next window boundary can overflow near Int64 max. No timestamp-domain validation.
findings.disposition: Decide supported bounds and implement consistently before documenting range/exception guarantees. Current docs can state seconds/default without promising all Int64 inputs.
findings.confidence: high for arithmetic, intended supported domain unresolved

findings.claim: Original aggregate response bytes have no explicit cleanup.
findings.evidence: Decoded TLVs own copies; disposing them does not clear response.RawData. Individual calculation siblings clear raw responses in finally; aggregate does not.
findings.disposition: Add failure-safe cleanup with success/malformed/custom-period followup failure coverage at closeout. Keep code-string lifetime separate.

findings.claim: Operation cancellation is converted to ordinary failure inconsistently.
findings.evidence: Broad Exception catches swallow cancellation in delete/rename/single-code/reset; bulk calculation propagates it.
findings.disposition: Extend existing OathTool cancellation followup; reconcile entrypoint exit/message policy and reset partial-success handling.

findings.claim: 1700000010 is ten seconds into a thirty-second window.
findings.evidence: The value is divisible by 30; assertions use the correct boundary.
findings.disposition: Correct comment only; preserve test values and assertions.

sources.sections: Instructions; LIST, DELETE, RESET, CALCULATE, CALCULATE ALL; no RENAME section
